lines: Mum, look! The lamps are switching on one by one. Like a queue!
That lamp went first. Then that one. It is a relay race!
Ping, ping, ping, all the way along. I can almost hear them.
Can I count them before they all light? One, two, three... aah!
Mum, the lamps are on. That does not mean bed. Does it?
The lamp by the kiosk is always last. He is a slow lamp.
Hello, lamps! Did you sleep well? All day?
My shadow just got a twin. One for each lamp!
The lamps are orange like apricots. Lit apricots.
I race the lamps. I lost. They are faster than Inès.
That lamp buzzed then glowed. It cleared its throat first.
Mum, are the lamps lit by a person? A very fast person?
I stood under one exactly when it lit. I am a lucky boy.
The lamps are on. I can see them from the stairs. Goodnight, lamps.
Lamps on means the dancing starts soon. I can feel it.
The sun is touching the sea! Mum! It is touching it!
Quick, look, before it goes! It is half a sun now.
It is a slice now. A slice of orange. Now a crumb.
Everyone stopped walking to watch. Even the gulls, I think.
Mum, the sun went red to say goodnight. That is polite.
Wait, wait, I want to see the very last bit. There!
The bay is pink and the sun is in it. Like a big bath.
If I squint the sun is a peach. If I wink it is a coin.
Who is on the other side getting the sun now? Lucky them.
Sunset is my third favourite thing. After laps and Biscuit.
I waved at the sun and it went down. It waved back. Sort of.
Bong! The church says eight. That means breakfast says now.
The bell! I counted eight. Papa, it is a breakfast bell.
Eight bongs. I was awake for all of them. A record!
The bell is up in the old town. It sounds like it is yawning.
Eight o'clock bell. Two hours to fountain time. Maybe less.
Twelve bongs! I counted with my fingers and two toes.
Mum, the bell rang twelve. Is that why the sun is so high?
Ding, dong, twelve times. The bell must be very tired now.
Twelve o'clock means citron pressé o'clock. The bell agrees.
Six bongs. The bell is saying goodbye to the afternoon.
The bell rang six! Who rings it? A man with a long rope?
The church bell sounds better over the water. It goes further.
Six o'clock. The sun heard the bell. It is getting ready.
One day I will climb up and see the bell. Up close. Hello, bell.
Mum! A star! Out the window! Can I stay up for the second?
There is one star. It is brave, it came out on its own.
Star number one. Nine hundred and ninety-nine to go.
Papa, the stars are out. That is the stars' morning, right?
The star is right above the fountain. It is guarding it.
I can see two stars from my bed. One each eye.
The stars came on like the lamps. Who switches those on?
Look, the star is blinking. It is winking at me, I think.
The moon is looking in my window. Goodnight, moon.
The moon made a white road on the sea. The sun had a gold one.
Is the moon following me? I moved my pillow. It is still there.
The moon is a night lamp for the whole bay. A big one.
{name}'s window just lit up! Hello, {name}! Welcome home!
Look, Mum, {name} is home. Their window just went gold.
I can see {name}'s light from my window. We are neighbours.
{name}'s lamp is on. Now I know where {name} is. Detective.
I counted the cups on the terrace. Thirty-one. Thirty-two!
So many people talking. It sounds like a big friendly bee.
Marcel is going so fast his tray is flying. Nearly.
Mum, we got the last table! We are very lucky people.
Clink, clink, clink. The spoons are playing a song.
The café is full of grown-ups. I am the only one running.
Lap nine. Café is busy. Lap ten. Still busy!
Everyone at the café is reading a newspaper. The same one?
The terrace is laughing. I can hear it from the fountain.
Marcel needs four arms today. I could be two of them.
When I zoom past the café, all the napkins go flap.
Shh, Mum. Listen. A hundred forks at the same time.
So many hats at the café! I collect hats. Eleven hats.
I can smell the café lunches from here. I am hungry by nose.
A croissant flake fell off a table. The pigeons cheered.
When it is this busy, citron pressé tastes extra pressé.
A full café means lots of people to watch my lap. Watch!
I can hear Marcel putting the chairs out. Scrape, scrape. Up!
The parasols are opening! Like flowers, but big and stripy.
Marcel is setting the tables. That means the day is real now.
From my window: Marcel shaking out a tablecloth. Flap!
Café chairs going out means holidays are still on. Yes!
Everyone is coming to the railing! It is a sun party.
Excuse me, can I go in front? I am small. Thank you!
So many people watching the sun. It must feel very famous.
I am saving Mum a spot. I am saving it with both arms.
Count the people at the railing with me. Nine. Ten! Me!
Mum, look at all the backs of heads. They are sun-watching.
Can we squeeze in? There is a Léo-shaped gap right there.
Should we clap when it goes down? I am going to clap.
Mum, lift me? Just a little bit. Over the grown-ups.
The man next to me said "beautiful". I said "I know".
The railing is full! I only fit one elbow. A good elbow.
Everybody's faces are orange. Mum, yours too!
A lady gave me her spot. I said merci. Twice, to be sure.
Why does everybody whisper at sunset? Is the sun shy?
The crowd is getting bigger and the sun smaller. Fair.
I am the youngest sun-watcher here. And the best waver.
The radio is singing me to bed. Second verse, then sleep.
A trumpet on the radio! I can do trumpet with my mouth. Bwaa.
I know this radio song. It goes la la la, and then la.
The radio and the waves are doing a song together. A duet!
The radio man said bonsoir. I said it back. Just in case.
Radio on, window open, pyjamas on. That is the evening plan.
Mum, dance with me? The radio is playing a dancing one.
If I listen to the radio with my eyes shut, is that sleeping?
The music started! Mum, I can hear the accordion from bed!
Tomorrow I stay up for the dancing. Tonight I listen. Deal.
The string lights are on and the music is on. Ooh, my feet.
Music! Somebody is about to do my robot move. Probably.
Accordion! That is the song where you go round and round.
The first dancers! I can see them from the window. Tiny ones.
First song! It is always the bouncy one. I know the order.
Someone is dancing all on their own down there. Bravo! Encore!
I can see the dancing from my window. I am doing it in socks.
Their feet go one-two-three. Mine go one-two-four. Close!
Mum and Papa dance later. I will dance it in my dream.
Look at them twirl! I invented that twirl this afternoon.
Next year I am allowed one whole dance. I asked. Mum said maybe.
The accordion goes in and out. It is breathing music.
Dancing outside, sleeping inside. I got the sleeping job.
Everybody dancing is smiling. I checked every face. Yes.
Bonjour, {name}! I am on lap six. Or seven. Wave!
Hello, {name}! Watch, I can run backwards. Nearly.
{name}! I found a shiny coin. Not touching it. Just saying.
There goes {name}. Walking slow, like grown-ups after lunch.
{name} smiled at my dancing. That is one fan. Two with Mum.
Bonsoir, {name}! Are you coming to watch the sun too?
{name} said hello first. I was just about to say it first!
I know {name}! I know everybody here. Nearly everybody.
{name} just went by. I counted the steps. Twelve. Long legs.
{name}, guess how many laps! No, more. No, more than that!
Mum, that was {name}. We are friends. We wave every day.
{name} walks like a person with a plan. I have a plan too.
Bon appétit, {name}! Are you having a citron pressé too?
Psst, {name}! The fish in here is called Paul. Pass it on.
Bonsoir, {name}! I am not going to bed. I am going for a walk.
Lucie! Ding ding! Can I ride on the back one day? One day?
Lucie! Is there bread in the basket? I can smell it is yes.
Whoosh! Lucie! When I am ten I am getting a bike. A red one.
Lucie, race me round the fountain! Okay, you won. Next time!
Lucie waved with one hand. ONE hand! On a bike! Wow.
Bonjour, Lucie! Say hello to the bakery from me!
Lucie does all her errands on a bike. I want errands now.
If Lucie's basket was bigger, I would fit. I measured me.
Lucie went by and all the pigeons went up at once. Flap!
Lucie has a bell and I have a whistle. Fweee. We are a band.
Inès! Race you! ...Next time. When my legs are longer.
Go, Inès, go! That is lap... I do not know. A big number!
Inès runs like the sunset is chasing her. Or she chases it.
Inès did a thumbs up at my dancing! I am a real dancer now.
Inès, are you racing the sun? Win, please! Go, go!
When I grow up I will run with Inès. Two laps. Then cake.
Inès goes pat-pat-pat. I go patapatapat. Mine has more pats.
Mum, Inès runs every evening. Can I run every evening too?
Inès! Your shoes are so bouncy. Are they made of springs?
Hi, Inès! I am practising too. Standing-still practising.
Inès is like a gull. Very fast and always looking at the sea.
Inès whooshed past and my hair moved. That is how fast.
Biscuit! Hello, Biscuit! He wagged at me. That counts as hello.
Biscuit has the waggiest tail in the whole town. Officially.
Yusuf, can I hold the lead? Just to the next lamp? Please?
Biscuit trots like he is late for a very important bone.
Mum, Biscuit looked at me. Twice. That is a sign about dogs.
Biscuit's ears go flip-flop when he trots. Flip. Flop.
Biscuit stopped to say hi to the lamp post. Lamps love dogs.
Biscuit, sit! ...He is too busy. Good boy anyway.
Henri and Odile walk in step. Left, right. A parade of two.
Odile, I did eleven laps! She said bravo. Two bravos!
Arm in arm is how grown-ups hold hands. I know things.
Henri walks slow for Odile. Or Odile walks slow for Henri.
Henri's cane goes tock on the stones. Tock, step, tock, step.
Odile knows everybody. She knew my name before I said it.
Forty-one years married! That is four of me. And a bit.
Odile winked at me. Then Henri winked too. A double wink!
Mum, when I am old can I walk like Henri and Odile? Slow and smiley?
Hei, Asgeir! That is Norwegian. I know hei and vafler.
Asgeir has a baguette. Everybody gets a baguette here. Rule.
Asgeir is walking and thinking. I can see the thinking face.
Asgeir! Watch my lap! ...He watched! Thumbs up!
Asgeir! Can I see inside the workshop one day? One peek?
Asgeir waved. They wave the same in Norway. I checked.
Asgeir says god morgen in the morning. Is it god golden now?
Asgeir, I played Fun Libs and the cat was very sticky. Ha!
Asgeir is going to the railing. Everybody goes at gold time.
Ding ding! That is Lucie. Everybody move! Not me, I am fast.
The bell! I can tell Lucie's bell from any bell in the world.
Ding! I wish I had a bell. I would ring it at pigeons. Nicely.
Lucie's bell goes ding-ding. The church goes dong. Town music!
Ding ding! The pigeons heard it too. Up they go!
That bell means Lucie. Or a very small church on wheels.
When I hear the bell I stop and be a statue. Like this.
A gull! He said kee-ow. I think it means hello, Léo.
Kee-ow! I can do it too. Kee-ow! The gull looked. He knows.
Gulls are alarm clocks that go off all day. That one is lunch.
Mum, that gull laughed. I did not even tell a joke yet.
Gull number one today! No, I forgot. Gull number forty.
The gull says the sun is still up. Thank you, gull.
A gull went kaaa over the water. That is gull for wheee.
That gull wants my citron pressé. No, gull. Mine.
That gull is calling his friends home for dinner. Crumbs.
Inès! Wait! No, do not wait. I will catch you at the corner.
Inès runs so fast her ponytail is always late.
When Inès runs past, the pigeons do a little hop.
Inès is racing the sun. I think she is winning.
Inès is resting at the railing. Her legs are having a holiday.
Inès is eating lunch. Even her fork looks fast.
Marcel carries four cups and not one wobbles. Magic hands.
Marcel walks in zigzags. Table, door, table. Like a game.
Marcel! Is one of those cups my citron pressé? Please yes.
Marcel has a tray of pink drinks. Grown-up lemonade.
Marcel has done a hundred trips today. I counted the first six.
Marcel winked at the tray. Or at me. Probably me.
Henri is reading the paper. He reads it very slowly. Fair.
Henri's cane goes tap, tap, tap. It is a slow drum.
Henri and Odile walk at the exact same speed. Practice.
Henri is giving the lemons a drink. Do lemons say merci?
Henri's watering can is bigger than my head. I checked once.
Henri! Can I do one pot? Just a little one? A tiny pour?
Henri has the smallest coffee. It is the size of a thimble.
Odile knows everyone. She waved at me AND my shadow.
Odile is holding Henri's arm so he does not float away.
Odile has tarte. Tarte at lunch! Odile is very wise.
Odile is telling Henri a crossword word. She is the boss of words.
Odile is pointing at the windows. She knows whose all of them are.
Bonsoir, Madame Odile! She said bonsoir back with a little bow.
Odile said I have grown since yesterday. I think she is right.
Yusuf is eating a sandwich and Biscuit is watching every bite.
Yusuf shared a crust with Biscuit. That is the rule of sandwiches.
Biscuit stopped to sniff, so Yusuf stopped too. Good team.
Yusuf told Biscuit to sit and watch. Biscuit is watching me.
Yusuf and Biscuit are both looking at the sun. Same face.
Biscuit's tail goes round like a propeller. He might take off!
Biscuit! Hello, Biscuit! He has four legs and they all wiggle.
Biscuit found a crumb. Biscuit eats biscuits. Is that allowed?
Biscuit is sitting at the railing like a little grown-up.
Biscuit is doing his best begging eyes. They are very good eyes.
Lucie! Ring the bell! She rang it! Best morning ever.
Lucie pedals so fast her basket flaps. Bye, Lucie!
Lucie's baguette sticks out like a flag. Team Bread.
One day I will ride with no hands. Lucie says not yet. Fair.
Lucie's bike is parked by the kiosk. It is resting its wheels.
Lucie is laughing at the drinks table. Her laugh goes ha-HA.
Mum is looking at her phone. I am looking at the fountain. Fair.
Mum! Look! No hands near the water! I am being very good.
Mum is walking round slowly. She is guarding me. Like a knight.
Mum ordered salade niçoise. I will borrow one olive. Shh.
Mum is looking at the arcade. I think she wants to play too.
Mum is leaning on the railing with her eyes half shut. Happy.
Mum says everything is golden. Even my knees. Look, they are!
Mum is doing her bedtime walk. I am doing my slow walk. Slowest.
Mum is not looking. Quick, one more look at the fountain.
Papa is on the phone by the column. He waved with his other hand.
Papa is telling a story at lunch. It has robot letters in it.
Papa has bread on his plate, bread in his hand. Very Papa.
Papa is walking around thinking about rosé or pastis.
Papa! Watch my jump! He is watching. He clapped. Twice!
Papa is at my railing. We are railing buddies.
Papa and Mum are clinking glasses. Clink means cheers.
Papa is laughing his big laugh. It makes the glass jiggle.
The workshop man is having coffee. He is outside! Amazing!
The builder is drawing on a napkin. Is it a robot? I hope it is.
I can see the builder in the window. He is making tools for robots.
The builder is at the arcade! Is he playing Fun Libs? Grown-ups can!
The builder is smiling at his phone by the arcade. A funny story.
Builder! What are you building? He said tomorrow. Tomorrow what?
The builder came out to see the sun. Even builders need sunsets.
The builder is at the railing. Ten minutes, he says. I am timing.
Asgeir is asking Henri about lemons. The lemons are fine, Asgeir.
Asgeir is standing by Henri's bench. He likes standing and talking.
Asgeir has a baguette! He is holding it like a sword. Nearly.
Asgeir, is your baguette warm? He said yes. I knew it.
Asgeir is drinking kiosk coffee. Lucie told him to. Good advice.
Asgeir is at the kiosk. I can see him from the dance floor.
Asgeir keeps stopping to look at the light. It is good light.
Asgeir is saying something to the sun. In Norwegian! It listened.
Asgeir and me both wave at the sun. We are a sun waving club.
Go, Inès, go! I am cheering with my whole arms.
Marcel put the bread down with a swoosh. Swoosh is a skill.
Marcel can see the whole café at once. He has café eyes.
Henri folded his newspaper into a square. Very neat. Very Henri.
Odile is stirring her coffee. Seven stirs. I counted.
Yusuf has a long lead and Biscuit uses every bit of it.
Lucie went round the corner and her bell came round after.
Mum has a pink drink and her happy shoulders. Night is coming.
Papa's phone call is mostly him saying yes and looking at gulls.
The builder said hello with his coffee. Coffee wave!
Asgeir walked past the fountain twice. Maybe he likes laps too.
The fountain splashes my left arm every lap. Only the left.
A pigeon is drinking from the edge. Small sips. Good manners.
My reflection is wobbly. He waves when I wave. Copycat.
Somebody threw a button in. Is a button a wish? A small one?
The top bowl spills into the middle bowl. It is sharing.
I go round this way. Clockwise. Clocks agree with me.
Lap twelve. The fountain is still in the middle. Good.
If I lean close, it sounds like clapping. For me, probably.
The wet stones are slidey. I run on the dry ones. Clever feet.
A leaf is going round and round the basin. Doing laps, like me!
Bonsoir, fountain. See you at ten o'clock tomorrow.
No bedtime for fountains. It just keeps going. Splish.
A blue marble is down there. I am not allowed in. I asked.
The water goes plip on the stone and plop in the bowl. Plip plop.
The pigeons step out of my way every lap. We have a deal.
Drops on my face mean I am going fast enough.
Shh, everybody. Listen. Now the fountain is the loudest one.
The spray is orange now. The fountain is making juice.
I dropped a petal in. It floated to the other side. Hello!
A bee is drinking here too. Bees get thirsty. I did not know.
Round the fountain is the best track. No corners. Only round.
Under the water my fingers go short and wiggly. Fish fingers!
A snail lives on the fountain. He does one lap a day.
The kiosk has a postcard of this exact fountain. Two fountains!
Newspapers pegged up like washing at the kiosk. Reading washing.
That kiosk window is a puppet theatre. When is the show?
Ice lollies in the kiosk freezer. I am only looking. Hard looking.
Lucie says kiosk coffee is the best. I say kiosk lollies.
The postcard stand squeaks when you spin it. One more spin.
Still open, the kiosk! Just looking, Mum. Only looking.
A comic with a gull on the front. My kind of comic.
Maps of the town at the kiosk! The fountain is on it. I checked.
After the kiosk there is only sea. End of the town. The edge!
Oranges! The kiosk smells of oranges today. Somebody had breakfast.
Ding! The kiosk counter has a bell. Ding means hello.
The post office never closes. Not for lunch. Not even for bed.
Robot letters go in there. I listened at the door. Quiet robots.
A letter to Biscuit from here: does it go in a robot bag?
The sign glows all the time. Like a night light for letters.
AI agents send emails from here. Do they lick stamps? No tongues.
Mum, the post office is still open! It is a night owl.
Dear post office, are you ever sleepy? Love, Léo. I will post it.
I patted the red letterbox by the post office. Good box.
It talks to about a hundred mail places. I only know Mamie's.
Bright sign means somebody sent a letter. I am waiting for one.
The arcade lights are chasing each other! Round and round, like me!
Fun Libs is in there. You give it a word and it goes silly.
My best Fun Libs word is wobbly. It fits in everything.
Bing-bong, says the arcade door. I made it go twice. Oops.
Every colour is on the arcade sign. Even ones I forgot about.
The bulbs blink one after another. Like a whisper going round.
In the daytime the arcade bulbs are asleep. They work nights.
The workshop light is on. Somebody is making something in there.
I can hear tapping in the workshop. Tap, tap, think. Tap.
Toolrails is being built in there. Is it a train? Mum says no.
The builder has a pencil behind one ear. That is how you tell.
Yellow window, person inside. The workshop is a lantern.
When I grow up I want a workshop. With a stool that spins.
Even in the daytime the workshop light is on. Busy busy.
I waved at the workshop window. The builder waved a screwdriver.
Being built, says the workshop. Is the sign being built too?
The library is having a rest. Only one lamp stays awake.
That one lamp in the library is my favourite lamp. Brave lamp.
I put my nose on the library window. Books, books, one chair.
Once the library wakes up, I will borrow the book about gulls.
The lamp is on for the books, so they are not in the dark.
People and robots will share that library. Who gets the comfy chair?
One chair by the lamp. A reading chair. It is waiting nicely.
I tiptoe past the library. Just in case it is dreaming.
Big brass handle on the library door. Shiny from all the hands.
I am waving at the sun with both hands. One is for the sea.
The waves come in to say hello and then go back. Shy waves.
Wrinkly sea, like Grand-père's hands. The nice wrinkly.
Way out there the sea stops and the sky starts. A line!
The breeze is blowing my hair straight up. Wind hair!
Blue, green, more blue. The sea is wearing stripes today.
I hold my ear out and the sea says swish. Then swish. Then swosh.
This is railing number four. My railing. Nobody told me, I know.
Sparkles all over the sea. Somebody spilled the glitter.
A cloud in the sea! No, a reflection. Two clouds!
How deep is the sea? Deeper than Papa? Papa standing on Papa?
Papa says the sea goes to other countries. Hello, countries!
Flat sea today. It is resting after the morning.
Light on the water jumps about. It cannot sit still either.
I stand on tiptoe and the sea gets bigger. Tiptoe works!
Same sea as yesterday, says Papa. It looks newer to me.
The sun is getting low. It is coming down to look at the sea.
Shoes on, laces double-knotted. The fountain is waiting for me.
Mum, can I go out? I have laps to do. Ten. At least.
I am stretching like Inès. Toes, knees, ready. Almost ready.
My legs woke up before me. They want to go round and round.
Snack finished. That means lap time. That is the rule.
Round two of the fountain! The afternoon laps are the fast ones.
I rested my legs for three whole hours. They are full again.
Paul the fish has missed me since lunch. Coming, Paul!
I will do one lap for every pigeon. There are a lot of pigeons.
Two more laps, then I sit on the edge and count coins.
Soon I can put my hot hands in the cold water. Best part.
After this lap I am going to look for Paul. Properly this time.
I need a sit down by the water. Not tired. Just thinking.
Next I am doing coin research. Very important. Very wet.
I am saving my last pebble for the fountain. One wish left.
Nearly twelve. My tummy has a clock in it. It says lunch.
In a minute: citron pressé. I am practising my please.
I want the chair that can see the fountain. Chair number five.
Marcel is going to say bonjour, young man. I can tell.
Lunch soon! I am going to ask for the bread with the holes in.
My fingers are wet. I will dry them on my shorts before lunch.
After lunch is quiet time. I will read about the long-necks.
Home soon, for a rest. I will rest very fast and come back.
Mum says quiet time. I will be quiet loudly in my head.
I am bringing a sugar cube home for later. For a horse, maybe.
Home after this. I am going to draw the fountain with Paul in it.
Our door is up that street. Twenty-two steps. I counted once.
Dance practice next! I have a new move. It has a name. The Gull.
Last lap, then over to the dance floor before anyone else.
My feet are warmed up from running. Now they can dance.
I am going to practise the spin until I stop wobbling. Or not.
The dance floor is empty now. That means it is all mine.
Tonight the grown-ups dance. So I practise first. To help.
Nearly six. Then I go and say goodbye to the sun. Every day.
One more twirl, then the railing. The sun likes a wave.
I must get to the railing early. The sun is slow, but I forget.
Done dancing. Now I go and lean on the railing like Papa does.
Last dance move, then I go watch the sea do gold.
Mum is coming. That means walking home slowly. My best slowly.
Bye bye, sun, I have to go now. See you tomorrow, same spot.
In a bit I walk with Mum and hold her hand. Only on the stones.
When we walk I will show Mum the cat with the white socks.
Mum is still looking at the gold. Then the long way home, I hope.
Bath next. I will make a bubble beard. A big one.
Pyjamas soon. The ones with the gulls on. Obviously.
Nearly bedtime. I am not tired. My eyes are just resting standing up.
When I get home I will tell my pillow about today. All of it.
Mum says bed. I say one more lamp. She says fine, one lamp.
I will leave my shoes by the door. Pointing out, for tomorrow.
Tonight I am going to dream about Paul. He will be big.
Papa is reading the next chapter tonight. Dragons, I hope.
Teeth, story, sleep. Then tomorrow comes. Fast, I hope.
The post office sign went bright! Somebody's robot wrote a letter!
Flash! Another email. Who are they all writing to? Their mums?
Bright again! Maybe that robot letter is going all the way to Norway.
The sign flashed. Quick, make a wish! Does that work on signs?
That flash means an agent sent an email. An agent is a robot helper.
An agent sent an email, I sent a postcard. We are both postmen.
Bright! I bet that robot wrote Dear Sir very, very politely.
The sign winked at me. I winked back. Both eyes, sorry.
Somebody's robot just did their emails. I want a robot for socks.
Mum! The sign! A letter went out and nobody even walked in!
The robots are still posting. Do they not have a bedtime either?
Bright! Somebody's agent answered a letter. Answering is polite.
I waved at the post office when it flashed. Letters like waving.
Another one! The robots must have very big families.
The sign went whoosh-bright. I am calling that a letter sneeze.
The sign flashed on this lap. That means this lap counts double!
Paul the fish saw the post office flash. He swam a bit faster.
Flash! I think that one was a birthday email. It looked happy.
How does the email get out? Under the door? Through the chimney?
The sign flashed right on my stamp move. It is dancing with me!
Mum, the post office flashed. Robots do emails at lunch too!
The arcade flashed! Somebody is filling in a Fun Libs right now!
Somebody just played Fun Libs! I hope they picked wobbly.
Arcade went bright! Somewhere a cat is wearing a silly hat now.
The arcade blinked. Somebody finished a story. Was it a funny one?
Bright arcade! I would put enormous spaghetti. Every single time.
The arcade flashed! I am doing a Fun Libs lap. A wiggly one!
Asgeir made that game when he was seventeen. I am nearly ten!
The workshop sign flashed! A robot borrowed a tool. Did it ask?
Workshop flash! That is Toolrails. One door and every tool inside.
